trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out up, right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So my guess (up from number 1) was wrong. Next I'll try right.
Going up would leave both cell (1,4) and cell (1,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Number 3 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Going right, the next 7 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 4. So the line goes down.
Going right would leave both cell (4,6) and cell (6,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,3). So the line goes down.
The line must go right: left is number 7, which comes later.
Going left would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going left would cut off the top-left corner (6 cells). So the line goes down.
Going left would leave both cell (4,1) and cell (6,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down would cut off the bottom edge (4 cells). So the line goes right.
Cell (5,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
